messages:
jordan (Eng, SF): Heads up — planning to move my homebase to Austin (TX) starting June 1. I will still be coming into the SF office 2 days/week for roughly 3 months while ramping. Quick Qs: how does the WFH stipend get handled for June (proration?), what do I need to do for payroll/state withholding, and do we need to worry about CA tax nexus for the company?
meera (People Ops): congrats! :tada: TL;DR: please submit the Change Homebase form (link below) and we'll coordinate payroll + stipend. Stipend proration depends on the number of days you are in each homebase during the month. Form: https://redwood.internal/forms/change-homebase (internal)
jordan (Eng, SF): thanks — can you give the proration math so I know what to expect?
meera (People Ops): sure. We pay the WFH stipend monthly. Simple proration we use internally: prorated_amount = monthly_stipend * (days_in_homebase / total_days_in_month). Example: if June has 30 days and you are in CA 10 days and TX 20 days, CA portion = stipend * 10/30, TX portion = stipend * 20/30. We'll apply the portion tied to your declared homebase for payroll records.
alex (Payroll): adding payroll context — once the Change Homebase form is in, Payroll will update state withholding to TX as your primary homebase. However, because you will perform services in CA 2 days/week, CA withholding may still apply for those pay periods. We ask folks to tag days in the timesheet with the state (example: "CA-day" tag) or put a note in the payroll comments for those pay periods so withholding is accurate.
meera (People Ops): action items for you: 1) fill the Change Homebase form, 2) add a comment on your first June timesheet noting the SF in-office days, 3) confirm travel schedule with your manager so we can estimate CA days for payroll. We will confirm final stipend proration on the June payroll cutoff.
sasha (Legal): quick legal note — short-term hybrid presence (2 days/wk for 3 months) typically doesn't by itself create a corporate tax nexus, but we track office presence and headcount in each state. If you or multiple employees are regularly performing work in CA consistently (or if you start doing client-facing on-site work), we escalate to Finance/Tax for a deeper assessment. I'll flag this to Finance for visibility.
payroll-bot: Reminder: Change Homebase form required within 5 business days of moving to avoid incorrect state withholding. Link: https://redwood.internal/forms/change-homebase
jordan (Eng, SF): got it — filling the form now and will add notes to June timesheet. thanks all! :raised_hands:
